title: Primary culture of tracheal aspirate-derived human airway basal stem cells
protocol: Remove the freezing vial containing 804G cells from liquid nitrogen and thaw it at 20°C–22°C.
Transfer the cell solution to a 15 mL conical tube and add 5 mL of neutralization medium.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 10–15 mL RPMI medium.
Plate the cells into a T75 flask.
Store the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Change SAGM medium daily.
Check the flask for proper cuboidal cell shape, confluency, and contamination.
If the cells have a proper shape, are 90% confluent, and show no signs of contamination, proceed to step 8.
If not fully confluent, change SAGM medium and check again after 24 hours.
Discard SAGM medium from the T75 flask.
Add 5 mL of 0.5% Trypsin to the T75 flask.
Incubate at 37°C until cells dissociate (5–10 min).
Tap the side of the flask lightly if cells do not dissociate after 5 minutes.
Check under the microscope to confirm complete cell dissociation from the flask.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 7 mL neutralization medium to the tube containing the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 10–15 mL SAGM medium.
Plate the cells into a T175 flask.
Store the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Change SAGM medium 1 day after seeding and every other day thereafter.
Monitor the flask daily for proper cuboidal cell shape and contamination under 5×, 10×, 20×, and 40× magnification.
Once confluency is reached, add 60 mL RPMI medium to the T175 flask.
Change media every other day for 8 days after reaching confluency.
Collect the supernatant every 2 days — this is the 804G-conditioned medium.
Sterilize the collected supernatant with a 0.22 μm vacuum filter.
Store the sterilized supernatant at 4°C for up to 1 month or -20°C for up to 1 year.
If the sample has an abundance of mucus, treat with 5 mL 0.1 mg/mL DTT in 1×PBS (from 10 mg/mL stock DTT solution).
Incubate for 5 min at 20°C–22°C under the hood.
Add 1×PBS to the mucus trap until the 5 mL mark to dilute the sample.
Mix well using a 1 mL pipette.
Place the 70 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL conical tube and lubricate with 2 mL PBS.
Pipette the sample from the mucus trap through the 70 μm cell strainer to the 50 mL conical tube (1 mL at a time).
Discard the cell strainer.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,500 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and the 804G-conditioned medium from the pre-coated T25 flask.
If the sample contains too many erythrocytes (indicated by a red cell pellet), add 1 mL of the red blood cell lysis buffer under the hood.
Incubate for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,500 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 5 mL SAGM medium.
Plate the resuspended cells into a T25 flask.
Store the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Change SAGM medium 1 day after isolation and every other day thereafter.
Monitor the flask daily for proper cuboidal cell shape and any possible contamination.
Check the flask under 5×, 10×, 20×, and 40× magnification to better visualize the cells and detect contamination.
Centrifuge the human TA sample after purification steps.
Remove the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellet in 80 μL MACS buffer.
Add 2 μL biotin-conjugated EpCAM antibody to the resuspended cells.
Mix the solution by horizontal hand shaking and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 30 min under the hood.
Add 2 mL MACS buffer to the cell mixture and centrifuge at 1,200 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellet in 80 μL MACS buffer.
Add 20 μL anti-biotin magnetic microbeads to the resuspended cells.
Mix the solution by horizontal hand shaking and incubate at 20°C–22°C for 15 min under the hood.
Set up the MACS column apparatus under the hood with a 15 mL conical tube underneath for collection.
Add 1.5 mL MACS buffer to the cell mixture and mix gently.
Add 500 μL MACS buffer to the column for initial lubrication.
Add 500 μL of cell mixture to the MACS column at a time.
Wait until 80% of the solution is filtered before adding the next 500 μL.
Repeat the process two more times until all 1.5 mL solution is filtered.
Quickly detach the column from the magnet and place it on top of a new 15 mL conical tube.
Add 500 μL of 1× PBS to the top of the column immediately.
Push the plunger down to release the solution into the 15 mL conical tube.
Check the flask carefully for proper cuboidal cell shape and cell confluency, as well as any possible contamination.
Discard the SAGM medium from the T75 flask and add 2 mL 0.5% Trypsin.
Incubate the flask at 37°C until the cells dissociate (5–10 min).
Lightly tap the side of the flask to force dissociation if needed after 5 minutes.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and add 4 mL neutralization medium to the tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and the 804G-conditioned medium from the T75 flask.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 10–15 mL SAGM medium.
Seed the resuspended cells into a T75 flask.
Store the seeded plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Change the SAGM medium 1 day after seeding and every other day thereafter.
Monitor the flask for proper cuboidal cell shape and any possible contamination daily.
Check the flask under a 5×, 10×, 20×, and 40× magnification to detect contamination.
Coat the 24-well inserts with 400 μL of 804G-conditioned medium.
Discard the SAGM medium from the T75 flask.
Add 5 mL of 0.5% Trypsin to the flask.
Incubate the flask at 37°C until cells dissociate (5–10 min).
Lightly tap the side of the flask if cells do not dissociate after 5 minutes.
Check under the microscope to confirm complete cell dissociation from the flask.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and add 7 mL neutralization medium.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL SAGM medium.
Aliquot 10 μL of the cell suspension and count cells using a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cells in SAGM medium to achieve a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Remove 804G-conditioned medium from each pre-coated insert.
Seed 300 μL of the cell suspension (3 × 10^5 cells) into the insert for a 24-well plate or 500 μL (5 × 10^5 cells) for a 12-well insert.
Add 150 μL SAGM medium to the insert for a 24-well plate or 1 mL SAGM medium to the well for a 12-well insert.
Add 750 μL SAGM medium to the well for a 24-well plate or 1 mL SAGM medium to the well for a 12-well insert.
Store the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Check under the microscope to see if the cells are confluent in the insert.
Refeed the cells with SAGM medium if they are not confluent by adding 400 μL SAGM medium to the insert and 750 μL to the well.
Replace the SAGM medium with PneumaCult medium containing inhibitors when the cells become confluent, using 400 μL for the insert and 750 μL for the well.
For a 12-well insert, use 500 μL of PneumaCult medium with inhibitors in the insert and 1 mL in the well.
Remove the medium from the insert one day after switching to PneumaCult medium and apply medium only to the well thereafter.
Change the medium daily for the first 7 days using PneumaCult medium with inhibitors.
Change the medium every other day from days 7 to 21, using PneumaCult medium without inhibitors.
Perform an apical PBS wash on days 14 and 21 by adding 400 μL sterile 1× PBS to the insert and incubating for 30 minutes at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Carefully remove the PBS from the insert after incubation without touching the membrane.
Remove the medium from BSC ALI cultures on day 21 of differentiation.
Add 400 μL 4% PFA in 1× PBS to the insert and 750 μL 4% PFA in 1× PBS to the well for cell fixation.
Incubate for 20 min in the dark under the hood.
Wash 3 times for 5 min with 1 mL 1× PBS in the insert and well.
Carefully cut half of the membrane from the bottom of the insert using a scalpel and blunt forceps, transferring it into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate the membrane in 10% sucrose in 1× PBS on ice for 1 h.
Incubate the membrane in 15% sucrose in 1× PBS on ice for 1 h.
Incubate the membrane in 20% sucrose in 1× PBS on ice for 1 h.
Incubate the membrane in 1:1 20% sucrose:OCT in 4°C for 10 h.
Add 1:3 20% sucrose:OCT to halfway fill a cryomold on dry ice, avoiding bubbles.
Check the flask for proper cuboidal cell shape and 90% confluency, as well as any possible contamination.
Discard the SAGM medium from the T75 flask.
Add 5 mL of 0.5% Trypsin to the flask without PBS wash.
Incubate the flask at 37°C until cells dissociate (5-10 minutes).
Tap the side of the flask lightly if cells do not dissociate after 5 minutes.
Check under microscope to confirm complete cell dissociation from flask.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 7 mL of neutralization medium to the tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL SAGM medium.
Aliquot 10 μL of the resuspension and count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Calculate the number of freezing vials required according to Table 2.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend in the appropriate volume of freezing medium to reach 1 million cells per 1 mL.
Aliquot 500 μL of the resuspended solution into each freezing vial.
Place each freezing vial in the Mr. Frosty and into −80°C for 12 h.
Transfer cells from the Mr. Frosty to liquid nitrogen the next day.
Remove the freezing vial from liquid nitrogen and thaw at 20°C–22°C.
Transfer the cell solution from the freezing vial to a 15 mL conical tube and add 5 mL neutralization medium to the tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant and the 804G-conditioned medium from the pre-coated T25 flask.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 5 mL SAGM medium and plate into the T25 flask.
Store the plate into a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Gently place the coverslip in the 24-well plate using sterilized forceps.
Remove the freezing vial from liquid nitrogen and hand-thaw it.
Transfer the cell solution from the freezing vial to a 15 mL conical tube and add 5 mL neutralization medium.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL SAGM medium.
Aliquot 10 μL of the resuspension and count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Calculate the volume of suspension required for each well based on cell counts.
Aliquot the calculated volume of suspension to a separate 15 mL conical tube.
Remove the 804G-conditioned medium from the pre-coated well.
Add the appropriate volume of the resuspension for each well and seed.
Add enough SAGM medium to the well to make a total volume of 1 mL.
Monitor the flask for proper cuboidal cell shape and contamination every day.
Check the flask under 5×, 10×, 20×, and 40× magnification.
Fix cells on the insert using 1 mL 4% PFA in 1× PBS for 15 minutes when the coverslip is 90% confluent.
Wash with 1× PBS for 5 minutes twice.
Transfer the plate out of the cell culture hood after washing.
Block the samples with blocking buffer stored at 4°C until expiration date.
Incubate samples with primary antibody according to standard protocol.
Incubate samples with secondary antibody according to standard protocol.
Stain nuclei with DAPI or another nuclear stain.
Add a drop of Fluoromount-G to a microscope slide for mounting coverslip.
Transfer the coverslip from the 24-well plate onto the microscope slide using forceps and pipette tip.
Ensure that the cell culture-treated side is placed down on the microscope slide.
Wipe the coverslip with a wet paper towel to eliminate salt precipitate before imaging.
Allow the coverslip to dry completely before imaging.
